cases.question: Are Memory Tax and MemoryTax one paper, and do they prove that summaries should replace original sources?
cases.source_scope: 31October authored selective/abstract review reports; not primary paper bodies.
cases.unresolved_support: No fresh primary read, replication, source-freshness or local-efficacy evidence.

windows.text:
| [Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34073v1) | Introduction, main result table, diagnostic sections, design implications, baseline and metric details | Paper reviewed selectively, not replicated |
| [MemoryTax: The Bitter Lesson of Agent Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29823) | Abstract | Different paper: one conversation, one run per cell; caption visibility confounds part of the comparison |

The broader Memory Tax paper compares eleven memory systems with a substantial
raw-history retrieval baseline: BM25 plus dense search and reranking, optionally
two rounds. Its diagnosis distinguishes information loss, retrieval difficulty
and reader/writer model changes. Source recovery alongside derived memory is a
useful design lead. This does not establish our local system's performance or
prove structured memory universally inferior. See its main table and sections
4, 6 and A.2 at the linked paper.

The smaller MemoryTax paper is a separate study, not a replication of that
eleven-system comparison. Its abstract explicitly discloses narrow sampling and
unequal photo-caption availability. Keep those limits attached to its headline.

Fresh primary-source review, 2 November 2026:
[RAW-RAG](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30755v1), method section3 and limitations6.1,
preserves source windows and uses dense retrieval plus cross-encoder reranking.
It reports first place in six of seven compared benchmark/model settings, and
explicitly limits its evidence to offline conversational tasks. It does not
establish our SWE/dev-ops performance or an operational state/permission system.

windows.text:
## Live smoke check, 26 October 2026

Primary source opened successfully:
[Linux Foundation AAIF announcement, 22 October 2026](https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/agentic-ai-foundation-announces-four-new-projects-agent-skills-open-responses-openenv-and-opensandbox).

| Probe | Access | Claim result | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| The announcement identifies Alibaba as the OpenSandbox contributor. | Readable publisher page; summary and New Projects section | SUPPORTED | Retain with citation. |
| Alibaba contributed OpenEnv. | Same genuine page | CONTRADICTED: it attributes OpenEnv to Hugging Face. | Correct the attribution. |
| The announcement proves coding performance improved 30%. | Same genuine page | NOT_SUPPORTED: no such measured result is reported. | Remove the number or find independent evidence. |
| A study at the synthetic path below proves all context loss is eliminated. | Browser tool could not open it; direct public HTTP request returned 404 | UNVERIFIABLE citation; claim not established | Do not cite or retain as fact. |

The last probe deliberately uses an invented test URL, not a real citation:
`https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/harness-memory-eliminates-all-context-loss-2026-study`.
The browser's access error alone was not called a 404; a separate HTTP read supplied
that status. These bounded checks demonstrate evidence handling, not universal
source coverage, automated semantic accuracy, or absence of hallucination.
